title: Nashville audition and first recording of Slim
summary: A Nashville club owner heard the band in Monroe and brought it up; they won a four-week contract and Slim recorded his first song, Feeling Sad, for a small label.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: So we did, we went on to that term. And the night we got there, Diana Watson and Illinois Jackie was playing. You can remember them, they were playing together. So after they went off, the show went off, and we came on, I don't know, people just went, they went wild and see that guy, that little boy in the main walking the bar with the guitar playing, and then that little boy would get on his shoulders and play together. So the guy told him, he said, man, you got a four weeks contract right now. So I said, well I can't play four weeks, I'll tell you, I can play the first week, I have to go back and play my one nighters out. I said, I'm going to play the first week, we'll take a four weeks contract, but I'm going to play one of them and come back. So he agreed for us. And after that we just stayed in Nashville, you know, off and on, off and on. So I met a guy who had a little record company, I can't think of the name of the record
company, but anyway, he had a record company there.

Yeah, I know who it is, but I can't call it. Yeah, so him and I got together, I said, name, how about Nick? No, the first thing was, Slim wrote a song in his hotel room. He wrote it on one of these laundry bags, remember the laundry bag, you'd be in brown paper. He wrote the whole song, he came in my room and sang the song to me. He said, what are you thinking about it? I said, it's all right. I said, you want to cut it? He said, yeah. I said, well, I'm going to talk to this guy who was at the club last night. He said, well, he said, so I got in touch with the fella, and so he said, well, look, man, I ain't got no money. He said, I'll press the record and release it if you pay the band off. I said, okay. So I bought the deal. He didn't have a studio. He had a big tape recorder, on there tape recorder. And he went somewhere and got some old bags, you know these bags where they put around, tighten them on the deal and tighten up, it's clean like a bag. And he had stuff all on the floor, all hung up beside the wall, just in that little room. With a small tape recorder, you know. And we cut the first session on Slim there. Feeling Sad. I tell the story. I remember the name. Ray Charles Cuttergold after he did. So that was the first starting of him.
